routes.label: Locate the face centers, prove disjointness and use sphere volume ratios

changes.rationale: Use regular tetrahedron vertices (+,+,+),(+,-,-),(-,+,-),(-,-,+) at coordinates +/-1. Its circumradius is R=sqrt(3), and each face is at distance r=1/sqrt(3). A face-exterior sphere of radius s has center distance r+s from the common center. Its farthest point is at radius r+2*s, so internal contact with the circumsphere gives s=(R-r)/2=r. Distinct face-exterior centers are 4*r*sqrt(2/3)>2*r apart; each is tangent externally to the insphere. Thus disjoint interiors yield uniform volume probability 5*(r/R)^3=5/27, closest to C. Reuse final separated-D volume probability and its local internal-contact proof. Do not silently use the pending F internal-sphere refinement.

answerCheck.reason: Regular tetrahedron vertices (+,+,+),(+,-,-),(-,+,-),(-,-,+) in coordinates +/-1 give R=sqrt(3), face distance r=1/sqrt(3). An exterior face-tangent sphere center is (r+rho)n. The furthest point from O has radius r+2rho; internal contact with the circum-ball gives r+2rho=R, so rho=r. Face normals have pairwise dot product -1/3; their centers 2r*n have pairwise distances 2r*sqrt(8/3)>2r. All four are internally tangent to the big sphere and externally tangent to the central sphere, so disjoint interiors give uniform volume ratio 5*(r/R)^3=5/27. Internal tangency is derived by the radial maximum, not imported from an external-tangency-only node.

routes.label: Derive the short-chord threshold through an isosceles altitude

changes.rationale: A radius chord has central minor angle pi/3, by bisecting the isosceles radius triangle and using sine at pi/6. Acute sine monotonicity then shows chord<r exactly for minor angle<pi/3. Pairwise short chords for three points force one cyclic gap greater than 5*pi/3: every gap must be either below pi/3 or above 5*pi/3, and three small gaps cannot sum to 2*pi. Hence there is one unique start of the short containing arc. Three disjoint anchor events each have probability (1/6)^2, giving 1/12, D. Reuse final separated-D arc probability with its precise right-triangle route; general-angle h091 is not used.

answerCheck.reason: Retain the D unique-cluster-start probability derivation and pending geometric-probability target. Replace h091 in its route: the isosceles radius triangle has an altitude bisecting the minor central angle theta, so chord=2r*sin(theta/2) by acute right-triangle definitions. Sine is increasing for theta/2 in [0,pi/2], and sin(pi/6)=1/2, so chord<r iff theta<pi/3. The remaining arc-length and three disjoint cluster-start cases are unchanged. This uses precise existing right-triangle and monotonicity scopes rather than a generic h091 application. A chord is shorter than the radius iff its minor angle is less than pi/3. For three distinct points the cyclic gaps must contain one gap greater than 5pi/3; otherwise all three would be less than pi/3 and could not sum to 2pi. Thus one unique start precedes the short containing arc. For each of three starts the other two independent points lie in the next one-sixth circle with probability 1/36. The cases are disjoint.
